writeup.1: Malbon’s Men’s Fall collection runs to eighty-eight pieces, which is more than anyone needs to look at. Twenty-seven of them carry the whole thing.
writeup.2: What holds it together is a named spine. Malbon built Ironworks Division out of heavyweight stone-washed hickory-stripe denim, the striped cotton that painters and railroad crews wore, and ran it across a jacket, a carpenter short, a pair of overalls, a sweatshirt, a snapback and a driver headcover. Antique nickel hardware and hammer loops carry through the lot, with the Division artwork across the back of the Foreman jacket. It is the least golf-looking thing Malbon has made.
writeup.3: Underneath it run three other threads. A stone-washed herringbone twill called Station covers a shirt, a pant and a cap. An all-over Inkwash print carries two windshirts and a short. The knits, Crosscut and Brickwork, do the quiet work the logos usually do.
writeup.4: Two collaborations close it out, and both are better than anything Malbon made on its own.
